document.quote: ADSL.STUDYID

clauses.note: The executable identifier is read from VS. The specification comment and the data guide name an ADSL merge, but ADSL1 does not supply this column.

document.quote:
The following core variables were merged from ADSL into all analysis datasets: STUDYID,
SITEID, USUBJID, TRTSDT, TRTEDT, AGE, AGEGR1, AGEGR1N, SEX, RACE, and
RACEN.

clauses.note: The data guide independently repeats the ADSL source for the core identifier across all analysis datasets; both ADVS row branches use the global VS derivation.

interpretations: The independent lookup reads published ../../data/adam/adsl.parquet and returns ADSL.STUDYID. It does not read adsl-yamaa.parquet or copy target REF.STUDYID as evidence.

Original matching keys STUDYID, USUBJID, VSSEQ and AVISIT stay unchanged from REF. The computed identifier is output as STUDYID__LITERAL so a putative identifier change cannot alter alignment. The ADSL lookup matches the preserved STUDYID/USUBJID and has no invented first/last rule.

Ordinary base rows use dataset VS and the global VS.STUDYID derivation. Added eot rows also use dataset VS and group by VS.STUDYID and VS.USUBJID; they do not override either identifier with ADSL or a different donor identity. The internal _USUBJID helper partitions endpoint ranking but does not replace the global output identifier.

ADSL1 joins the derived ADSL input on STUDYID/USUBJID and keeps a first record for other subject attributes. The two identifier columns bypass that lookup in both row paths. The literal uses the documented published ADSL source without copying that first-record policy.

The REF base preserves every ordinary and added End of Treatment row. Joining ADSL as a lookup does not rebuild, filter or duplicate either branch, and the data guide states no observed/derived exception to its core-variable merge.
claims.assessment: Define-XML and the data guide identify the published ADSL source; the executable ordinary and endpoint paths take this identifier from VS. Pilot 6's reimplementation advs.r (lines 108-113) starts from VS and merges ADSL by STUDYID and USUBJID, so its identifier is the VS value matched to ADSL.

The shared AVISIT codelist enumerates telephone weeks and Weeks 4-24, but enumeration alone does not require ADVS records at every shared-codelist visit.
The native ADVS structure is one record per subject, parameter, analysis visit and analysis timepoint; eot groups by subject, test and timepoint before assigning the endpoint label.

The retained sources do not settle how to recognize on-treatment vital-sign assessments relative to treatment dates, whether an unscheduled/early-termination assessment is an endpoint candidate, residual ties, or absence of a postbaseline candidate.
The data guide limits analysis datasets to enrolled subjects. No enrollment criterion is invented from source labels; subject inclusion is a shared dataset-row review question.

The first whole-variable probe is withheld instead of presenting an observed-only visit map as the complete rule. Any future computed AVISIT probe must use AVISIT__LITERAL and preserve the supplied AVISIT matching key.
claims.assessment: Collected-visit labeling is specified, while the implemented endpoint selection departs from the retained Week 24 and on-treatment conditions and leaves material choices unresolved. Pilot 6's reimplementation advs.r (lines 147-168) title-cases VS.VISIT except screening, unscheduled, ambulatory ECG and retrieval visits, then adds End of Treatment as the last record by ADT, AVISITN, ATPTN and AVAL among records with AVISITN > 2, with no Week 24 upper bound or on-treatment test.
claims.question: Which retained EOT definition governs ADVS: designated Week 24/early-termination visit or last on-treatment assessment on or before Week 24? Specify candidate visits, the on-treatment date test, repeated-assessment tie handling and no-candidate behavior; also confirm enrolled-subject selection.
claims.not_probed_reason: A whole-variable literal rule must cover both observed and derived End of Treatment records. The retained definitions differ in designated-visit versus last-on-treatment eligibility and do not specify the operational treatment-date test, early-termination/unscheduled candidate handling, residual ties or no-candidate behavior. Using current REF.AVISIT, borrowing the executable latest-mapped-visit rule, or probing only observed records would not independently state the complete documented rule.

claims.not_probed_reason: The retained exact text specifies flag meaning and exclusions but does not operationally define the complete eligible set for every parameter/visit/timepoint and ordinary versus added End of Treatment row. In particular it does not settle whether every remaining scheduled value is analyzable, the handling of missing values and repeated assessments, the vital-sign within-visit selection/tie rule, or the endpoint on-treatment test, designated early-termination/unscheduled candidates, residual endpoint ties and no-candidate behavior. The general Week 24/early-termination endpoint wording and the vital-sign last-on-treatment wording also require reconciliation. A literal whole-variable probe cannot borrow the present _AVISIT_OUT condition or latest-mapped-visit selection as an unstated policy. Copying REF.ANL01FL, assigning Y to every nonblank REF.AVISIT, or supplying only the explicit exclusions would not independently establish the complete flag rule. No such formal partial probe is claimed.
interpretations: Ordinary rows use dataset VS and map only BASELINE and the listed scheduled weeks through Week 26. Every resulting nonblank _AVISIT_OUT receives Y without a separate AVAL availability, subject-population or within-visit selected-record condition. Excluded source visits remain in the dataset with a blank flag.

The eot branch also reads VS. It groups source fields including VSSEQ and assessment details, partitions rank by subject/test/timepoint, orders only by mapped visit number descending, filters rank=1 and source analysis visit number greater than 2, and assigns End of Treatment. The global ANL01FL condition then assigns Y to each emitted endpoint. No secondary date/sequence criterion is authored to resolve equal-ranked endpoint assessments.

SAP Section 8.2 actual-date windows and the closest-to-target/equidistant-before-target rules are scoped to the named efficacy instruments and laboratory assessments. The data guide selected-assessment/LOCF paragraphs concern ADQSADAS, ADQSCIBC and ADQSNPIX. They do not supply a vital-sign tie or carry-forward policy.

The baseline and missing-safety statements do not authorize imputation or a guessed missing-value flag condition. SAP Section 9.2 uses Visit 3 for baseline weight/BMI and Visit 1 for baseline height in demographic summaries; this does not silently override the ADVS per-visit screening exclusion or establish parameter-specific ANL01FL applicability.

The safety-population labels govern the cited displays. They do not expressly require an ANL01FL guard using SAFFL; a population restriction is therefore not invented for the flag. The data guide enrollment restriction is a dataset-row scope issue rather than an instruction to flag existing screen-failure records.
